No Morrowind plate was consulted and no art-direction reference was crossed with a fidelity one. The art-direction question about these characters (do they read as Saxhleel rather than generic lizardmen) is real and is NOT judged here.

score.band_label: The owner's transparency complaint was diagnosed correctly for the first time and measurably closed, and the reuse mechanism is the best-evidenced thing in the visual tree. But the anti-gaming guard on the metric that carries the whole claim misses the deletion of both the character's hands, the animation half of the child was not built, and on hardware the characters read as white plastic mannequins.

status_reasons: The 3% silhouette guard — the only anti-gaming guard on the crack metric — does not catch deleting both of the character's hands: 178 -> 123 crack px (-31%) at -0.31% silhouette drift, against a 3.0% threshold. Demonstrated on a patched copy of the source tree.

The guard's own docstring justifies 3% by citing -1.0% for the whole of this build's change; the measured figure is -2.9%, so the guard's real headroom against the arm-deletion cheat is 0.4 percentage points, not the margin claimed.

The surviving discriminator in actor-orbit-holes.mjs computes `held` from the unfiltered ring, so one stray pixel of a weapon or shield vetoes a whole pocket — the stray-pixel guard the file describes two lines earlier was applied only to the branch that is reported and not to the branch that is gated.
The builder's documented reproduction command crashes at HEAD (--baseline-ref=HEAD patches nothing), so the headline 9,254 -> 2,204 cannot be re-derived as written. The correct baseline is a1d24f58.
The plan's orbit row is binary — zero background pixels — and is unmet; the instrument's own verdict on the shipped build is FAIL, at both profiles.
Plan item 4, the clip set, is untouched: CLIP_NAMES is empty, no authored crossfades, no root-motion agreement measurement.
On hardware frames at the two mandatory character close-ups, neither the player nor the NPC reads as a character: no skin tone, no face, arms not separable from the torso, hands not visible as hands.

biggest_gap.what: The anti-gaming guard on the character defect metric is a scalar silhouette-area check, and a scalar cannot notice that a named part stopped existing. Deleting both of the character's hands — palms, three fingers and an opposed thumb each — improves the headline crack metric by 31% and moves the guarded quantity by 0.31% against a 3.0% threshold. It is not caught.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Every claim this piece makes about the character rests on the crack metric, and the crack metric's only defence against being gamed has now been shown, on a copy of the source tree, to miss the cheapest realistic mutilation. The builder's two declared cheats — delete a whole arm, swallow the arms into the torso — are the conspicuous versions and they are caught. The version a builder under schedule pressure would actually reach for is deleting the small expensive parts, and that walks straight through. The plan's own item 5 calls hands one of the two features a person looks at first.
evidence: hide-both-hands: 178 -> 123 crack px, silhouette 53075 -> 52913 px (-0.31%), NOT CAUGHT
hide-hand (one hand): 178 -> 137 crack px, silhouette -0.14%, NOT CAUGHT
shipped build's own drift against baseline a1d24f58: -2.9%, against a guard docstring claiming -1.0%
hide-arm, the builder's own control: -3.3%, caught by 0.3 percentage points
biggest_gap.remedy: Replace the scalar with a per-part presence census, and keep the area guard as its second half. rasterise() already carries owner[] and the part label, so classifyPockets's caller can record the set of part names contributing at least one pixel anywhere in the run and fail any build whose part set is a strict subset of the baseline's. That is roughly a dozen lines, it introduces no new threshold to argue about, and it catches deletion of any named part at any size. Keep the 3% area guard for the opposite direction — it is what catches weld-arm-to-rib, which adds rather than removes. Then re-run the six existing controls plus hide-both-hands and record that all seven behave.

secondary_observations.what: The successor of the discriminator mistake the builder was asked to find: `const held = ring.some(...)` at actor-orbit-holes.mjs:350 is computed on the unfiltered ring, while the stray-pixel guard described in the comment at line 351 is applied only to `major`, which feeds `allJointed` — and allJointed is explicitly reported rather than gated. One pixel of a held object bordering a pocket removes that pocket from the crack count. Remedy: compute held from the same 15% share the file already chose, then re-run the full profile and report whether 2,204 moves.

One of this critic's own controls was inert, and the reason corroborates the build. sink-crest — burying the dorsal crest further inside the body and shrinking it 65% — returned numbers identical to the shipped build to the pixel, because the crest is already fully interior to the skinned surface. The control proves nothing about the guard and is reported as inert rather than as a pass, but it is independent confirmation that defect #2 (four cones floating up to 35 cm off a 14 cm-deep back) is structurally closed rather than cosmetically hidden.
evidence: sink-crest: 178 crack px, 53075 px silhouette — identical to shipped

secondary_observations.what: The 12 Deck motion sequences are not an instrument for judging character animation as configured. All twelve ran on hardware, 12 ok / 0 red, 400 frames, deterministic — but the character occupies roughly forty pixels of frame height, so the contact sheets can show that a sword arcs and a body translates and cannot show whether a knee bends or a foot slides. This is a W1-30V finding, not a W1-30D one, and it means the animation axis above is scored on the absence of the work rather than on frames that failed.

The reuse claim is verified independently and is the strongest thing in this piece. 17 characters on one body plan, 17 distinct structural keys, 0 duplicates; widening the shared humanoid plan by 6% on a copy moved exactly 15 of 17 — 9/9 saxhleel, 6/6 humanoid, 0/2 quadruped — which is the written exemption behaving rather than a miss. The prediction was made before the run and came true. Colour is correctly excluded from the distinctness measure, on the grounds W1-30K established independently.

secondary_observations.what: game/index.html's import map, edited outside the builder's owned paths and flagged loudly by the builder, was checked and is as described: additive, inert, and `grep -rn "from 'three'" game/src` returns nothing so no existing module resolves through it. Not a defect, and the builder was right to flag rather than bury it.

method_deviations: The 144-frame orbit (24 stops x 3 distances) was NOT rendered on hardware. The Deck's char-player and char-npc setups are one yaw each, and the orbit is a separate rig this critic did not build. Every transparency statement in this verdict is therefore 'clean at the stops rendered', not 'clean at 144 stops' — and that distinction is exactly the one the owner's original complaint turned on, so it is stated rather than smoothed.
The full 5,760-frame profile was not re-run after diagnosing the held-object bug, so this verdict makes no claim about how much of the 2,204 that bug is hiding.
The beast and undead families were not independently re-measured; the builder's 640-frame figures are taken as reported.
No naive character pack and no silhouette-readability pack were built, for the S51 reason recorded against RI-VIS06.

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is FALSE and the misses are itemised in method_deviations: the 144-frame orbit, the full-profile re-run, the beast/undead families, and the RI-CAM07 duel traces. blind_done_where_required is FALSE: Protocol A did not run because pack-builder and judge must be different agents and this critic is one agent; that is recorded against RI-VIS06 with score null and measured not_measured rather than being scored as a pass or quietly omitted. judged_output_not_source is TRUE — every claim about the build was taken from a run of the instrument or from a hardware frame, and the two source findings (the held-object rule, the crashing reproduction command) are findings ABOUT the instrument, which is the one thing a critic must read as source. The guard finding was produced by patching a copy of the source tree and running the unmodified instrument against it, never by a flag inside the instrument.
